See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola is ready to welcome Harvey Elliott back into the fold after a 'difficult' season away from Anfield.

Elliott spent last season out on loan to Aston Villa under manager Unai Emery but only managed to bank 109 minutes of action.

And speaking in his first press conference since taking the reins from Arne Slot this summer, Iraola was full of praise for the 23-year-old’s work ethic.

Iraola said: ‘Harvey is here with us, I have seen him with the eagerness to show up, get super ready, he’ll have a chance in pre-season, we’ll need him and it’s a good sign.

‘I hope we can see him in a good place. I think Harvey comes from last season. [It] had to be difficult for him; strange situation. They couldn’t even play him, and I think he uses this experience - the bad situation - to make himself even more eager to be a Liverpool player.’

An obligation to buy clause built into the loan agreement with Aston Villa meant they would be forced to buy Elliott for £35 million once he reached a certain number of appearances for the team.

Harvey Elliott only managed 109 minutes of action for Aston Villa during his loan spell last season

He is now back with Liverpool hoping to prove he can be a part of Andoni Iraola's side

To avoid the financial hit, Emery kept Elliott on the bench for the second half of the season.

Speaking to reporters in May, the Villa manager apologised for the ‘embarrassing’ situation that cost Elliott a year of development in a key stage of his career.

Emery said: ‘My apologies for Harvey Elliott, is every day in my mind. But it is [about] responsibility. We have our responsibility and Liverpool have their responsibility.

‘Of course, it is something embarrassing for everyone involved. As a human and as a person, how the season has gone has been difficult.’

Elliott has an opportunity to get back on track with Iraola’s arrival as the Spanish manager looks to sign more players and boost the squad in the absence of top players such as Hugo Ekitike and Mohamed Salah.

Two signings have already been made, with Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz joining Liverpool.

Sports.title: Inside the unlikely rise of Djed Spence: The reason Fulham let him go as a teen, an act of kindness that won over Ange Postecoglou, how Thomas Frank improved his game and why Tuchel thinks 'trouble-maker' is perfect supersub
Sports.content:
A straggler on the halfway line as Wonderwall was queued up, Djed Spence turned to the dugout and sought out England coach Justin Cochrane. Pointed over with feeling and saw that reciprocated. That was for the hours and hours at Tottenham and now with the Three Lions.

His manager, Thomas Tuchel, came sauntering over. The pair shared a moment of celebration when all eyes were diverted towards another emotional rendition of Oasis in front of England’s sea of supporters at the Hard Rock.

Later, as Spence headed inside after seeking out his sisters in the family enclosure and doing his bit during the post-match sing-song, the England backroom staff welcomed him into a mass cuddle. The 34-minute appearance was certainly the finest of his international career, and perhaps his career in general.

Spence was the man Tuchel needed as Norway pushed and probed, looking the more likely in the humidity of Miami as England threatened to wilt.

His pace was key in getting his side up the pitch, his tenacity in closing down the opposition – including Norwegian keeper Orjan Nyland, nearly leading to a goal – gave others a chance to breathe. He had one shot that was parried by Nyland, keeping Norway on the back foot, he won a penalty only for it to be overturned by VAR. It all helped turn the momentum back England's way.

Can Spence lay claim to being the first part-time left back labelled a super-sub in a major competition? It feels highly likely. And deserved. Tuchel will want more of that in Atlanta against Argentina on Wednesday.

Djed Spence used his energy and drive to pressurise Norway when he came on in Saturday's quarter-final, and he almost forced keeper Orjan Nyland into a costly mistake

Spence (centre) joins in with his team-mates' celebratory rendition of Wonderwall after England's victory in Miami

Spence's touchmap shows how regularly he bombed forward against Norway (England attacking left to right)

The make-up of a successful tournament team needs all sorts and a squad player at full back whom Tottenham almost jettisoned two years ago amid fears over his attitude stood up for the cause and delivered when it mattered most on Saturday evening. These are the little stories that a World Cup throws up.

Only three players recorded more defensive contributions than Spence on the night – and they all started. Spence was everywhere, winning the war with a dangerous Oscar Bobb and powering England on from left back with an energy they had been so desperate for. From driving forward to spotting interceptions to nicking possession in the very final seconds as Norway built an overload, Spence was everywhere.

It is little wonder that Cochrane – his former coach at Tottenham under Thomas Frank – and the wider staff recognised this as Wonderwall faded away in one of those unseen slices of togetherness they will cherish.

They see the work, the way Tuchel berates Spence during training sessions to really squeeze the best from a 25-year-old whose stock continues to grow. They see rapid improvement and a player well integrated in this group, obvious when gatecrashing a recent Morgan Rogers press conference to pose a question on who is the quickest in their stable.

As part of the defensive reinforcements in Mexico and then Miami, Spence’s importance to how Tuchel is navigating a way through these knockout stages is clear to see and it is evidence as to why the coach picked specific players for specific moments. A slightly crazed Tuchel told the defender to ‘cause trouble’ as he geared up to enter the Floridian heat and he followed those instructions to the letter.

The dynamic between the two of them has presented intrigue throughout the tournament, notably after the barracking during the first few minutes of training early in the World Cup, consisting only of gentle passing drills.

‘Djed! Djed! Djed! Wake up! Wake up!’

It didn’t appear to be particularly solid communication between a manager and trusted player, more like a naughty schoolkid, but is the sort of stick that is elevating Spence to new levels. The player has suggested that his hunger and character have progressed since a first call-up last August.

Is Tuchel tougher on him than anyone else? ‘Yes. He likes me I guess. It’s perspectives. It’s just his way of managing,' said Spence. 'Maybe he believes I can do more and reach new heights.’

Spence also won a penalty for England against Norway, only for VAR to overturn the referee's decision

'It’s just his way of managing,' said Spence of Thomas Tuchel's intense style. 'Maybe he believes I can do more and reach new heights'

Spence was born in Kensington, west London, to a Jamaican father and Kenyan mother and his elder sister is the actress Karla-Simone Spence. His girlfriend Gabby Jolie has been out in the States supporting him, along with his sisters.

He started out at Fulham but was released as a teenager and taken on by Middlesbrough, who would sell him to Spurs in 2022. But he's had a nomadic career for a 25-year-old, with loans to Nottingham Forest, Rennes, Leeds and Genoa.

Tuchel did due diligence on the full back, whom Neil Warnock famously warned could be playing in non-League if he didn’t improve his dedication to the game. When not out on loan while at Spurs, Antonio Conte could not jive with him and despite Spence’s undoubted popularity at the club, the unforgiving Italian quickly became exasperated at a failure to listen to instructions.

Ange Postecoglou also publicly referenced ‘attitude’ in training – a reason why Fulham let him go – and openly admitted that were it not for injuries around December 2024, then Spence would have been on his way out a month later.

As it was, he played his way in – seemingly a turning point coming down at Bournemouth when he had not even featured.

Deep in a row with travelling supporters following a 1-0 defeat, Postecoglou was left to it by the majority of Tottenham’s squad, who instead sought refuge inside. Spence went over, put his arm around the manager, and led him back to the dressing room. He was in the side a fortnight later and never looked back.

There is definitely more of an awareness about staying engaged, shaped by a number of managers in recent seasons. Frank spent weeks fine-tuning his recovery runs, making sure he doesn’t simply switch off when attacking moves break down.

The focus on those basics has helped Spence's game – and is probably one of very few victories Frank took from Spurs.

Thomas Frank (right) helped Spence with some of the basics of defending, such as improving his recovery runs

Spence has been wearing protective headgear since breaking his jaw - though he dispensed with it during extra time in Miami in a bloody-minded display of courage

When Spence had ignored Frank on the pitch after defeat by Chelsea last season, a hugely embarrassing episode all round, he realised how poorly it had reflected on his coach and made sure to make a full apology in his office. For somebody so relaxed, there can be complexities with Spence.

But Tuchel knows that consistency comes from staying well on top of him: history with others tells him as such. It is why Spence, laidback to the point of being horizontal, has learned to accept the harsher criticism, aware that it improves him and improves England.

Off came the headgear protecting his broken jaw – Liam Delap’s handiwork – during extra time in Miami. The mask kept slipping due to the heat and Spence – who isn’t thought to be required to wear it anymore – ploughed on unfettered.

A bloody-minded display of courage. One that underlined his significance within this England squad. Because if this week is to go down in the annals, then Tuchel needs a Spence or two.

Sports.title: What I learned from Andoni Iraola's note-perfect Liverpool unveiling: How he'll avoid traps Arne Slot fell into, his hint on club's transfer plans and why I was blown away by new Reds boss, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
What I learned from Andoni Iraola's note-perfect Liverpool unveiling: How he'll avoid traps Arne Slot fell into, his hint on club's transfer plans and why I was blown away by new Reds boss, writes LEWIS STEELE

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

AI is taking over at Anfield and, funnily enough, Andoni Iraola’s first official engagement as Liverpool boss felt like artificial intelligence had really arrived.

Not because he was robotic in his body-language and words, as some managers are. Anything but. Instead, it was because everything he said was note perfect, as if he had been programmed to only give inspiring, well-informed and measured responses.

It is easy to fall into the trap of falling for every word a new boss says, of course. The first press conference is always a chance for some easy wins: say a few buzzwords and the supporters will be salivating, especially this fanbase which has been eager for change.

Former Bournemouth boss Iraola knows that as much as anyone and recognises that his words mean diddly squat if they aren’t backed up with results on the pitch. Yet, as far as opening addresses go, the Basque nailed it.

Daily Mail Sport was in the room and has picked out some of the biggest talking points from the man tasked with turning around Liverpool’s fortunes after a dismal campaign cost Arne Slot his job...

Andoni Iraola was officially unveiled as Liverpool's new manager today - and everything he said was note perfect

The Basque boss gave well-informed and measured responses that will have been music to Liverpool fans' ears

Words to fill fans with confidence

It won’t make the same headlines as Jose Mourinho declaring himself ‘The Special One’ or even Jurgen Klopp insisting that he wanted to turn Liverpool ‘from doubters into believers’ but Iraola’s first words will be worth looking back on next spring.

‘I would like to give them (the fans) a team they can feel proud of,’ he said when asked about his objectives. ‘I think football and especially Liverpool is about connecting.

‘Connecting with the people, connecting with our supporters. I've been on the other side at Anfield. I’ve experienced the goal that (Federico) Chiesa scored on the first day of the season (against Bournemouth last year).

‘You can feel the stadium, I would love to have this every time we play but that has to come from us, inside the pitch. We have to be a team that works hard, intensely, aggressively, vertically so everyone can be identified and everyone can feel comfortable supporting this team.’

Last season, Liverpool fans – even the most hardened Slot backers – could not feel too much pride watching a team with a weak defence and uninspiring attack.

Even when they won matches, they were hardly thrilling displays that got bums off seats, while Anfield became less a fortress and more a place where teams would rock up and fancy their chances – the Reds won just 10 of 19 home games, compared to 14 the year before.

Iraola wants to change that and intends to do so with a high-octane style of play, though the 10 home draws he managed at Bournemouth might not go down too well here if that were replicated.

Iraola wants to get Liverpool fans excited with a high-octane style of play, having experienced a raucous Anfield atmosphere on previous trips with Bournemouth

'We have to be a team that works hard, intensely, aggressively, vertically so everyone can be identified and feel comfortable supporting us'

Righting the wrongs of Slot

For 12 months, Slot could have walked into any bar in Liverpool and received a free pint (not that he would, as he kept a low profile). He was a hero and fans loved him after he brought them some of the best days of their lives with the Premier League title win of 2024-25.

For the next year, though, he was better off keeping his head down. From hero to zero in the eyes of many. By the end, pretty much everything the Dutchman said and did was criticised, some of it justifiably and some of it unfairly.

Whenever a manager has been sacked, the new guy can achieve some small wins. ‘Manager X reverses ban on ketchup,’ is the usual headline, soon to be followed a year later by ‘Manager Y bans ketchup at the training ground’.

But Iraola said some things in this press conference that suggested he will do things very, very differently to Slot.

For example, the Basque insisted he wanted to get a true feel for the city of Liverpool, immersing himself in the culture and taking some pictures.

He said: ‘I would also like to go to the city, experience the city: I know some places, I would have to take some pictures. But it's also part of the magic of being the Liverpool manager and I would like not to change too much.’

See you in PopWorld on Friday night then, Andoni? Maybe not, but this approach delighted fans after Slot decided to live in Cheshire, away from the hubbub of Liverpool.

It may seem an unreasonable stick to beat a manager with, added to the fact Slot was criticised for spending lots of his days off with family back in the Netherlands, but it is something the supporters care about.

Iraola's first press conference suggested he will avoid the excuses that caused his predecessor Arne Slot (left) to come under fire from fans

Not here to make excuses

Another thing Slot was criticised for was how, in the eyes of outsiders, he would be full of excuses. He would often complain about injuries, referees and how his team struggled to convert chances into goals against stubborn defences.

Iraola, though, insisted: ‘I prefer to face low blocks. We’ll be in control of the game, we’ll concede less chances and spend a lot of time in the opposition half. Those are the scenarios we have to face.’

Instead of complaining, the new boss says he is looking forward to working out how to unlock teams who come to defend.

Relaxed, personable demeanour

You need not be a body-language expert to read Iraola’s mood on Monday morning: grinning like a Cheshire cat, plenty of toothy smiles, polite hand-shakes, eye-contact, trying to answer all questions rather than side-stepping them (that might not last!) and all done in a relaxed manner.

He came across as a likeable individual and that can only be a positive thing for all concerned, be it staff or players.

Iraola was also prompt and took his seat at exactly 11am, not a minute early and not a minute late. It’ll keep the broadcasters happy at least.

Ready to give youth – and Harvey Elliott – a chance

Several first-team players were at Liverpool's HQ on Monday, including new defensive signing Jeremy Jacquet, Iraola’s ex-Bournemouth charge Milos Kerkez and a few youngsters looking to impress the new boss.

Harvey Elliott has already been back for a week, having trained with the Under 21s, and he will be given a chance to prove himself this pre-season.

Iraola said Harvey Elliott (pictured) will get a chance to impress in pre-season following his disappointing loan to Aston Villa

His former Bournemouth player Milos Kerkez (pictured) will be another out to impress on tour in the US

The 23-year-old signed for Aston Villa last summer on a loan deal that would become permanent when he made 10 appearances. It was seen as a foregone conclusion he would be staying at Villa Park for good but it never came to fruition as it was clear Unai Emery did not fancy him.

Now Elliott is back and Iraola said: ‘I’ve seen him with this eagerness to show himself, to get himself ready again. He will have a chance during the pre-season, we will need him.

‘Harvey, last season had to be very difficult for him, because it was a strange situation where basically they couldn’t even put him in to play.

‘I think he uses what he has experienced, the bad situation, to make him even more eager to be a Liverpool player.’

Youngsters will also be given chances to impress under Iraola this pre-season, with the squad to travel to Chicago next Monday. The Reds play three friendlies, with the tour also taking in Nashville and New York.

Calmed fans over quiet transfer window

Liverpool fans are an anxious bunch at the best of times, always hungry for news updates. The fact this summer has been rather quiet in terms of transfer rumblings has sent some poor souls into overdrive.

Iraola calmed fears that they might be going to go into the season undercooked, though, by saying: ‘We've signed two players (Jacquet and winger Victor Munoz). We need more, we know this.

‘We are working on this. As a coach I want the players here from day one, selfishly, but we know it doesn't work like this, we're working hard for those signings.’

Iraola impressed in his first briefing. Now it is time for the higher-ups to provide him with a competitive squad with a few fresh faces. Next stop Chicago.

Sports.title: Aston Villa transfer briefing: The four wingers on radar, why club were stung by bargain Youri Tielemans release clause, the players Unai Emery would happily let go and what double sale means for Morgan Rogers' future
Sports.content:
What a 24 hours for Aston Villa fans.

On Sunday night they were celebrating a possible £60million club-record deal for Swiss star Johan Manzambi, who wants to move to Villa instead of Newcastle.

On Monday morning, they were feeling gloomy again as it emerged Youri Tielemans was set to join Manchester United and Daily Mail Sport revealed that Lucas Digne could move to Paris Saint-Germain after the World Cup.

Because Villa find themselves in UEFA's ‘special measures’, they must offset the cost of signings with sales. Other than simply sticking with the same squad, Villa have no option but to let some key players depart.

Here Daily Mail Sport breaks down the choices Unai Emery faces – and the detail within UEFA’s rules that gives them a little more breathing space.

On Sunday night Villa fans were celebrating a possible £60million club-record deal for Swiss star Johan Manzambi (left), who wants to move to Villa instead of Newcastle

Youri Tielemans is set to join Manchester United after they activated his release clause

UEFA’S rules – the state of play

Before analysing Villa’s window, it is worth remembering the terms of UEFA’s ‘settlement agreement’, which European football chiefs imposed on the club when they broke spending rules.

Villa are allowed to lose £52m in wage and transfer spending across 2025-26 and 2026-27 as long as billionaire owners Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens inject at least that much during the relevant period. They fulfilled their side of the bargain with a £93m share issue in the 2024-25 accounting period.

Now for the next part, which requires a close look at UEFA’s club licensing and financial sustainability regulations. When Villa sign players, they can spread the cost of the transfer over five accounting years. In that scenario, Manzambi would cost £12m for each of the next five years.

For player sales, however, clubs can write down the entire sum immediately. So in the case of Tielemans, who joined on a free transfer, that would be an instant profit of nearly £35m – the value of his release clause. Digne’s release clause is nearly £10m, but that is a little more complicated.

Digne joined Villa for £25m in 2022 and signed a new three-year deal a year ago, when his ‘book’ value for accounting purposes was £10m. That will now have dropped to about £6.5m. By selling Tielemans and Digne, Villa could write down a profit of nearly £42m, putting them at least £30m in the black even if Manzambi joins, taking into account the £52m they are allowed to lose.

Digne and Tielemans are also among Villa’s highest earners, which would ease the strain on the balance sheet even more. Then if Villa can offload unwanted fringe players such as Lewis Dobbin, who is set to join Southampton, Unai Emery can breathe a little easier.

Yet replacements never come cheap and Emery is unlikely to be happy with these developments. With the Premier League starting again in a little more than five weeks, Emery and his lieutenants have plenty of work to do to give him a squad who can compete at home and abroad.

Lucas Digne joined Villa for £25m in 2022 and signed a new three-year deal a year ago, when his ‘book’ value for accounting purposes was £10m

Unai Emery has plenty of work to do in the transfer market to keep Aston Villa competitive

Emery’s response

Three of Emery’s favourite words are ‘serious’, ‘mature’ and ‘responsible’. Think of three to describe Tielemans and Digne, and they will be near the top of the list. They are high-performance, low-maintenance footballers – consistent, rarely injured and respected across the squad.

Yet Digne turns 33 on July 20 and Tielemans will be 30 next year. The Belgian has also been playing top-level senior football since he was 16. How much more does he have left in the tank?

Given fellow central midfielders Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali have moved for nine-figure sums this summer, the release clause in Tielemans’ deal feels remarkably low. Yet when Villa signed him in summer 2023, they had qualified only for the Conference League and the midfielder market was very different to how it is now.

A release clause – plus very high wages – likely ensured the Tielemans deal made it over the line. Still, though, charging only £35m for a proven performer seems almost negligent. Even though he is 29, to think Tielemans could cost only a third of what Declan Rice, Anderson and Tonali did is quite a head-scratcher.

At the start of this summer, Emery’s focus was on wide attackers. Ibrahim Mbaye, the Paris Saint-Germain forward, remains high on his list, as does Jarrod Bowen of West Ham. He also likes Harvey Barnes and Gabriel Martinelli but priorities may have to change.

With Tielemans possibly on his way out, Amadou Onana sidelined with a ruptured ACL and Boubacar Kamara still recovering from his own knee injury, Villa are short of experience and quality in the middle. Expect that to be addressed as a matter of urgency.

Villa's Amadou Onana ruptured his ACL while on World Cup duty with Belgium

Boubacar Kamara is still recovering from his own knee injury, leaving Villa short in the middle of the pitch

Will other players be sold?

Put simply, yes – assuming Emery wants to strengthen. Manzambi is a thrilling prospect but at this stage, does not appear to have the tactical discipline to play in central midfield for Emery and Freiburg used him mainly as a No 10.

At left back, Ian Maatsen has never quite convinced Emery and Villa have been offered the chance to sign Pervis Estupinan, the former Brighton defender currently at AC Milan. Emery would probably rather have sold Maatsen than Digne but Maatsen is only 24 and may improve.

Tammy Abraham joined Villa only last January but never forced his way past Ollie Watkins. Don’t be surprised if Abraham is among those Emery considers expendable, though finding a buyer may be a trickier task. The same is true of Evann Guessand, who spent the second half of last season on loan at Crystal Palace.

The one deal that could give Emery freer rein in the market, however, is the one Villa would really, really rather not do.

Tammy Abraham joined Villa only last January but never forced his way past Ollie Watkins and could be sold

The Morgan Rogers issue

Villa know they are going to receive bids for their star attacker this summer. They also know that, despite signing a new deal less than a year ago, Rogers would be open to a move. Arsenal are believed to be strongly interested.

Yet Villa chief Nassef Sawiris has watched players he deems less valuable than Rogers, like Tonali and Anderson, command fees of £100m and more. He and co-owner Edens see no reason to offer discounts on the 23-year-old and the likely sale of Tielemans and Digne will strengthen their hand.

The nightmare scenario for Villa is that Arsenal test their resolve with a bid well in excess of £100m in mid or late-August. That would unsettle the player and, if Villa decided to accept, upset the balance of the squad, leaving little time to source a replacement of similar quality.

Players who deliver double figures in goals and assists are very precious and even if Manzambi fulfils his enormous potential, he will need time to adjust to the speed and physicality of English football.

Villa will hold out for north of £100m for England star Morgan Rogers having seen the likes of Sandro Tonali and Elliot Anderson go for large fees this summer

One more issue to follow closely: the negotiations for Tielemans mean that lines of communication between Villa and United are firmly open.

The clubs have done business before, too – Marcus Rashford had a successful loan spell at Villa in the second half of the 2024-25 season and might have signed up for another year’s loan had they qualified for the Champions League. The less said about Jadon Sancho’s stint at Villa Park, the better.

Rashford, though, is worth watching. A return to Villa would be complicated. His £325,000-a-week wages are more than double those of Villa’s top earners, leaving another loan as the only realistic option. Would United be happy to strengthen a fellow Champions League qualifier?

As things stand, though, Barcelona have not moved again for Rashford and if there is no place for him at United, Villa may at least be tempted to pick up the phone.

Sports.title: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso reveals he has held crunch talks with midfielder Enzo Fernandez after Real Madrid's brutal snub - and hints that Alejandro Garnacho has no future at Stamford Bridge
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso has spoken with Enzo Fernandez and wants the Chelsea vice-captain to stay for next season despite the 25-year-old Argentinian appearing interested in a summer switch.

Alonso was unveiled in the Drake Suite at Stamford Bridge on Monday afternoon after starting work on his four-year contract. One of the topics of discussion centred on Fernandez, who has been the source of so much speculation that Real Madrid released a statement on the rumours.

Real are known to be among his admirers, though the La Liga giants managed by Jose Mourinho insisted they are not in talks for Fernandez, who is valued at £120million by Chelsea.

‘Yes, we have spoken,’ Alonso said when asked about the Argentina international who is set to face England at the World Cup this Wednesday. ’As you can understand, it remains private, but we have spoken.’ When pressed on whether he wants to keep Fernandez, Alonso said: ‘Yes.’

Chelsea are getting to work in the transfer window, having sold Marc Cucurella to Real for £47.5m, Tyrique George to Everton for £22m, and Andrey Santos to Manchester United for £50m. Santos’ switch was confirmed on Monday, shortly before Alonso’s unveiling.

Xabi Alonso has discussed the futures of Enzo Fernandez and Alejandro Garnacho after he was unveiled at Stamford Bridge on Monday

There has been intense speculation surrounding the future of Enzo Fernandez this summer while the midfielder has been away on international duty with Argentina

‘We need to make important decisions, right decisions,’ Alonso said. ‘We have a strong base already built. Now we have to build and build this mentality, to be competitive on the pitch, to win games and enjoy it. We are ambitious. It is important we build the right mentality to compete. I am optimistic to think we will have a great season.’

Cole Palmer has returned to pre-season training, which started on Thursday, after being excluded from Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for this World Cup.

Alonso said the 24-year-old Englishman has returned in the ‘mood’ for a ‘great season’.

‘We have had a few training sessions already,’ Alonso said on Palmer. ‘From the first day, you can see he's a special talent, a special player. It's not easy to have one of those. You can notice his quality, how he's able to play, the right decision in the right spot.

‘So I'm happy that he has come in a good mood, a good mindset to have a great season, and we are really looking forward to getting the best from him.

‘If we are able to build a strong team with the proper stability to find the key players, for sure, Cole is going to be one of those key players in the attacking part.’

Alejandro Garnacho looks destined to leave Chelsea this summer

As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Alejandro Garnacho has not returned for pre-season because he is for sale after a single season. Alonso also confirmed: ‘The situation is we've spoken with the sporting directors. There's interest in him from other clubs. It hopefully finishes in the best way for all parties.’ Garnacho was signed from Manchester United for £40m last summer.

Alonso was unwilling to reveal whether he will be prioritising a back three or a back four, with the new Chelsea boss saying: ‘For sure I have something in mind. This is my job. We want to be active, brave, play good football, compete well, but above that, we need good mentality.

‘That’s fundamental to understand what to do and what it takes in each moment. We want to show that we are ready to go. Once we are closer to the start of the season, we will reassure that with all the players.’

Sports.title: Arsenal keeping tabs on PSG winger Bradley Barcola and admire Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers - as Unai Emery's side finalise club-record deal to sign Johan Manzambi after hijacking Newcastle move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa want Estupinan

As mentioned this morning on Window Watch, AC Milan’s Pervis Estupinan is on Aston Villa’s radar.

The 28-year-old Ecuador international left-back is one of a number of targets being assessed by Villa should Lucas Digne re-join Paris St Germain, as reported by Tom Collomosse.

AC Milan and Ecuador defender Pervis Estupinan is on Aston Villa’s radar this summer

RB Leipzig move for £21m Burnley star

Burnley defender Maxime Esteve is due at RB Leipzig’s training ground later this week for a medical ahead of a £21million transfer.

The 24-year-old centre back has agreed to the move which will be ratified pending his medical.

Highly-rated Esteve has impressed since joining from Montpellier in 2024. His deal will also include add-ons.

Burnley defender Maxime Esteve is due at RB Leipzig’s training ground this week for a medical

Wolves leave £23.4m star out of Portugal training camp

Wolves forward Tolu Arokodare has been left out of their squad for the pre-season training camp in Portugal.

Wolves have rejected loan bids for the player from Fiorentina and Trabzonspor, while a number of other clubs are also interested.

Arokodare cost Wolves £23.4million in September and had a dressing room bust-up with Mateus Mane last season.

Fiorentina are expected to return with an improved bid for Arokodare, who has ruled himself out of a move to Trabzonspor.

Wrexham target Premier League goalkeeper



Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson has emerged as a target for ambitious Championship side Wrexham.

Club to club talks are underway over a possible deal but there are other teams showing an interest in the 26-year-old.

Patterson is valued around the £7million mark and spent the second half of last season on loan at Wrexham’s promotion rivals Millwall where he made 14 appearances as they narrowly missed out in the play-offs.

Wales star targeted by Sheffield United

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo

Sheffield United are weighing up a move for Wales international Rabbi Matondo.

The 25-year-old former Manchester City and Rangers winger is with Brann in Norway but they have told him he is free to leave and he his looking to return to the UK.

Former Leicester star training at Sheffield Wednesday

Former Leicester City winger Wanya Marcal is training with Sheffield Wednesday.

The 23-year-old former Portugal U20 international is a free agent after his contract expired at the Foxes.

Nathaniel Chalobah is also training with Wednesday again after his contract with the club ran out at the end of the season.

Winks set for Italian job

Harry Winks is in Italy completing a medical ahead of his move to Cagliari

Harry Winks is in Rome today ahead of his medical with Cagliari.

The Leicester midfielder is set to sign a two-year contract with the Serie A side.

The 30-year-old former Tottenham star watched Leicester’s 3-0 pre-season win over Northampton on Saturday but was expected to leave after Cagliari agreed terms last week.

Leicester are in throes of adding attacking midfielder Conor Chaplin, formerly of Ipswich, on a free and ex-Southampton goalkeeper Alex McCarthy, also a free.

Santos completes switch

Manchester United have completed the signing of Andrey Santos from Chelsea for £50m.

The agreement is £48m plus £2m in add-ons. Chelsea will also retain a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

Andrey Santos has joined Manchester United from Chelsea

United announced the signing with a video of the Brazil midfielder wearing the the club's shirt and saying: 'Since when I was young, I dreamed of this moment.'

Santos becomes the first signing with Michael Carrick as head coach.

Read the full story here.

Tigers on the prowl in transfer market

Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic has confirmed interest in Croatia internationals Marco Pasalic of Orlando City and HNK Rijeka’s Toni Fruk, plus Hajduk Split’s Rokas Pukštas, a USA Under-23 international.

The three are on an extensive list of targets being worked on by the Premier League new boys who expect to confirm Okan Ozkan as their new sporting director over the next 48 hours.

The Tigers have been in talks with Ozkan, who had been working at Polish club Pogon Szczecin. But the Polish club’s Canadian owner Alex Haditaghi sparked a social media spat with his Hull counterpart Acun Ilicali.

Haditaghi threatened legal action over Hull’s approach for Ozkan, in a succession of messages, whilst copying in the Football Association and Premier League.

Hull still expect to sign Oscar Zambrano from sister club Maribor, and are agreeing a £3m deal to sign Mjallby’s Swedish World Cup left-back Elliot Stroud.

Gunners keeping tabs on Barcola

Arsenal still remain attentive to Bradley Barcola’s situation at Paris Saint-Germain.

They also admire Aston Villa’s Morgan Rogers and accept both will be expensive to prise away.

Arsenal remain attentive to the situation of Paris Saint-Germain and France winger Bradley Barcola

Liverpool also admire Barcola. He is one of a number of wide attackers being assessed by the club but they are yet to make a formal enquiry.

Arsenal are awaiting Leandro Trossard’s decision over his proposed move to Besiktas.

The Gunners have a deal lined up for Christos Tzolis from Bruges which they may accelerate when Trossard leaves.

Another player that is on Arsenal’s radar but lower down their list is Norway’s Antonio Nusa.

The RB Leipzig winger had a decent World Cup on the back of making 35 appearances in the Bundesliga last season but there have been concerns about his knee condition since a move from Bruges to Brentford collapsed on medical grounds in 2024. A specialist later cleared him to play and he joined Leipzig.

Meanwhile, midfielder Christian Norgaard is attracting interest from Saudi club Al Jazira.

Dobbin closes on Southampton move

Aston Villa forward Lewis Dobbin is closing on a £9million move to Southampton.

The 23-year-old scored 10 goals on loan at Preston last season and was also wanted by Wolves, Middlesbrough and Sheffield United. Villa will receive further add-ons based on performances and appearances.

Villa forward Lewis Dobbin is closing in on a move to Southampton

Villa, who are finalising a club-record deal for Freiburg midfielder Johan Manzambi, have also been offered the chance to sign Pervis Estupinan from AC Milan.

The 28-year-old left back previously played for Watford, Brighton and Villarreal.

Sports.title: France 'don't have any French players', claims Spain's former prime minister in racist attack on the eve of World Cup semi-final
Sports.content:
France 'don't have any French players', claims Spain's former prime minister in racist attack on the eve of World Cup semi-final

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

France has been given added motivation to beat Spain in their World Cup semi-final after a racist attack by a former Spanish prime minister, who implied none of the team are French because so many are people of colour.

The comments by Mariano Rajoy, a week after a Paraguayan senator launched a nakedly racist attack on Kylian Mbappe, have provoked outrage in France. In an opinion piece published by the newspaper El Debate, Rajoy said: 'They have a top-level squad. That said, they don't have any French players.'

Spanish players have found themselves having to disown the statement ahead of their clash with France.

Defender Pau Cubarsi said: 'If they play for the French national team, they are French, regardless of their skin colour. We must show tolerance towards everyone, because we all deserve respect.'

Striker Borja Iglesias added: 'I can understand that he didn't say it with bad intentions, but we need to be more vigilant about this kind of remark.'

The French Embassy in Spain also condemned Rajoy, issuing a factual rebuttal that noted all 26 players of Didier Deschamps' players are French citizens and 23 of them were born in France.

France's football squad, led by Kylian Mbappe, is facing another racism row during the World Cup after a former Spanish prime minister said the team doesn't 'have any French players'

Former Spanish prime minister Mariano Rajoy expressed his controversial view in an opinion piece published by the newspaper El Debate

The France squad are said to have viewed the politician's comments with bemusement, but a second racist attack on them in as many weeks is likely to fuel their resolve to beat Luis de la Fuente's team at the Dallas Stadium and reach a third successive World Cup final.

The players' siege mentality was strengthened after a round-16 game in which France beat a cynical Paraguay team when that country's senator Celeste Amarilla attacked Mbappe as a 'colonized Cameroonian, pretending to be French – resentful, nouveau riche, arrogant and ugly'.

The French captain called her 'a despicable woman, unworthy of her office' and the Paris prosecutor's office has opened a judicial investigation into Amarilla.

Bizarrely, she then said was considering suing Mbappe for 'gender-based violence'.

The latest attack contributes to a sense that France is under siege from opponents at the tournament.

The French nation also felt slighted when Argentina criticised the appointment of a French referee, Francois Letexier, for their game against Egypt.

Kylian Mbappe called senator Celeste Amarilla 'a despicable woman, unworthy of her office'

Mbappe's forthright response to Amarilla two weeks ago was admired by team-mates, though there is far greater motivation for France's players in comments Lamine Yamal made about the prospect of playing the world's No1 side.

Yamal, whose parents were born in Morocco and Equatorial Guinea and who is regularly the target of racist attacks in his own country, said: 'We beat France in our last two matches. If France should be afraid of anyone, it's us.'

Ibrahima Konate responded: 'To be honest, we don't listen to what's being said. We mustn't be afraid of anyone.

'We must remain humble and not fall into that trap, especially at this stage of the competition. He can say what he wants.

'We're going to try to prepare as best we can. And at the end of the match, we'll see who benefits.'

Sports.title: Brendon McCullum reveals 'tap on shoulder' as he breaks silence on England Test axe
Sports.content:
Brendon McCullum reveals 'tap on shoulder' as he breaks silence on England Test axe

Brendon McCullum saw his time as England test head coach come to an end last week after three years in the role and he has now spoken out on the decision for the first time

View 2 Images Brendon McCullum was sacked last week (Image: Getty Images)

Brendon McCullum has revealed he got a ‘tap on the shoulder’ before his England Test sacking last week. McCullum, 44, had been in charge of the red-ball side since 2022 but the ECB confirmed that he had ‘stood down’ in a statement.

‌



McCullum’s exit came after a dismal run of seven defeats in nine matches, with England having suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat in the Ashes over the winter in that time.

‌



Speaking about the decision to move him on, McCullum has confirmed that he was given a nudge before being pushed. He said: “Yeah, I got a tap on the shoulder.

‌



“I was disappointed but at the same time I fully respect the decision. We’re in a results business and fundamentally our results weren’t good enough. It’s time for someone else to have a go.

“We didn’t always get it right. For that, I put my hand up and say we weren’t able to get there.”

Brendon McCullum sacked as England Test coach as future of white-ball job decided READ MORE :

And while McCullum was disappointed to lose his role, he further suggested that England’s recent form was a reason why he has been moved on.

‌



He added: “We just weren’t quite able to win those big series, against India and Australia, the two marquee series. We just weren’t able to get the results and for that I guess I can only say sorry.

“I was the leader of that group. I was in charge of the team culturally, in charge of the team tactically, in charge of the team results-wise as well.

View 2 Images Brendon McCullum will still be in charge of England's white-ball side (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“If you don’t get the results, being a results business, fundamentally you get replaced. I’m not unaccustomed to that, I’ve been around this game for 20-odd years and I know if you aren’t getting the results, someone else needs an opportunity. I put my hand up for that and accept it wasn’t good enough.”

McCullum will still be involved with England by staying on as the side’s white-ball coach. On the split coaching set-up, the New Zealander said: “Once the new coach comes into play we will sit down and unpick a lot of this stuff.

“You’ve got different staff, players, schedules are different, obviously captaincy discussions, but it’s about what is right for English cricket. I’m sure that will be a collaborative process. I also wish the new Test coach all the best.”

Sports.title: Conor McGregor provides fresh injury update after making retirement decision
Sports.content:
Conor McGregor provides fresh injury update after making retirement decision

The 'Notorious' has confirmed he will require surgery after suffering a nasty knee injury against Max Holloway at UFC 329 on Saturday night

View Image Conor McGregor after his loss to Max Holloway at UFC 329 (Image: Cooper Neill)

Conor McGregor has confirmed he will undergo surgery after vowing to continue fighting after his brutal loss to Max Holloway.

‌



The 37-year-old ended a five-year hiatus on Saturday night against the former featherweight champion - 13 years on from their initial fight. On that night, McGregor would go on to win on points, but was unable to claim the bragging rights for a second time this past weekend.

‌



McGregor suffered an injury to his right knee just seconds into the contest after he landed rather awkwardly after attempting a switch kick. The Dubliner fell to the canvas multiple times after, before the referee eventually waved off the bout just 69 seconds into the opening round.

‌



The Irishman has vowed to continue fighting despite suffering his third loss in a row. He was seen limping out of the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas - with reports suggesting he was on his way to hospital. On Monday, McGregor provided fans with an update, stating that he will in fact need surgery, and has doubled down on claims he will fight again.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

Max Holloway reveals exactly what Conor McGregor told him before UFC fight was stopped READ MORE :

"Surgery. Prehab. Return to martial arts practice. Go again. Final fight of the contract. Please God!" he said. The statement read: "My faith is unconditional and I am thankful I get to prove it! My lifestyle changes are permanent and not just until. I am thankful I get to prove it.

‌



"I am in sin city and remain completely devoid of all sin. I will not open that door nor crack its seal! I am already back to collecting wins! In Jesus name I pray! Church was intense today, my heart is heavy but through Christ my mind is STRONG! I am so grateful to see my family fall more in love with God each day!

Conor McGregor brutally trolled by UFC rival after losing comeback fight READ MORE :

"I am a child of God. I am a friend of God. God makes a way for me where there seems to be no way. I am not a victim of my circumstances, I overcome them. God is at work in me to will and to work his good pleasure! My youth is being renewed like the eagles! In Jesus I am thoroughly loved, cherished, adored. I walk in divine health. I live under supernatural protection.

‌



"All things work out for my good! All things are possible for me because I am a believer! I trust in You Lord! Show me Your way. Thank You God."

Heading into the clash on Saturday night, McGregor had two fights left on his second deal - with his final fight already pencilled in to take place next April. But many within the MMA fraternity feel as if the UFC icon is spent.

However, should he decide to make another comeback, Holloway has welcomed a potential trilogy meeting. "After turning around so fast for this fight in March, it's been fast," he said.

Article continues below

"But I'd love to see this Conor 170lb domain that he was talking about. This different world he was talking about. I want to see what his injury is first, but I then want to come back again in 2027. I will take some time to have a break to see my family, and then you guys will see Blessed return in 2027."

Sports.title: Conor McGregor has return questioned after Max Holloway loss
Sports.content:
Conor McGregor has return questioned after Max Holloway loss

The Irishman has promised to make a return to the cage after injuring his knee just 69 seconds into his latest comeback, but UFC legend Daniel Cormier has poured cold water on McGregor's comments

View Image LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JULY 11: Conor McGregor of Ireland falls after sustaining an injury on a kick in the first around against Max Holloway of the United States in their welterweight bout during UFC 329 at T-Mobile Arena on July 11, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) (Image: Getty Images)

Conor McGregor has vowed to make another return to the Octagon, but UFC legend Daniel Cormier questions whether the fans would get behind the Irishman again.

The former two-division UFC champion ended a five-year hiatus on Saturday night when he took on Max Holloway - 13 years after their initial encounter. On that night, McGregor would go on to win on points in Boston, but their rematch played out rather differently.

Just seconds into the opening round, McGregor appeared to have injured his knee after throwing a spinning kick and landing rather awkwardly on his right side. The 37-year-old did his best to continue, but after falling to the canvas on multiple occasions, the referee eventually waved off the clash after just 69 seconds.

Immediately after the underwhelming contest, fans had suggest that the Irishman was carrying an injury going into the fight. However, McGregor insisted he was fit, and promised he would be back. “I was so sharp and so ready for this fight I cannot believe what has happened," he wrote on social media.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

Max Holloway reveals exactly what Conor McGregor told him before UFC fight was stopped READ MORE :

"The talk of me being off while walking in to the fight is nonsense. I was calm, ready, and confident. I am in shock what has taken place. The devil is literally staring at me right in front of my face here. I am not engaging. I will be at church tomorrow. I will overcome this. I will not be deterred. I will return."

Despite McGregor's insistence he will fight again, Cormier has his doubts. "The question now becomes does Conor McGregor have it in him to come back? That is a big ask," Cormier said on his YouTube channel. "It's big of us to ask Conor McGregor, if his knee is blown out, to go through another year of rehab, another year of the sacrifices, the pain that it takes to work yourself back to a professional mixed martial artist – especially when you have the money that Conor McGregor has. That's a big ask.

"And if you ask me truthfully, I am more likely to tell you that it's not going to happen than it will happen. He's very unique, and I think the whole week showed that he's the biggest star we have. The whole week showed that. I just wonder if he even does try to come back once again, do people even buy into it again and say they want to see Conor McGregor go at it one more time? It really sucks, as well, because the card itself was insane."

Conor McGregor brutally trolled by UFC rival after losing comeback fight READ MORE :

Fans criticised McGregor's decision to throw a kick right from the word go, but Cormier was quick to leap to the defence of the Dubliner. “There have been times when people did crazy things to start a fight, and they worked," he said.

"I remember Fabricio Werdum ran across the Octagon and superkicked Travis Browne like he was in the game Double Dragon. Jorge Masvidal did it to Ben Askren. Sure, everyone's mad because it went sideways. But if Conor had landed it, everybody would've praised him.”

The Irishman's coach, John Kavanagh, echoed Cormier's comments, saying: “Devastated,” he wrote on social media. “That opening jump switch kick was drilled daily for months, multiple times in warm up. Never an issue. Knee went when he threw the very first kick. Doesn’t get any worse than this. Looking forward to seeing my family in a few days.”

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua undercard finally revealed ahead of comeback fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua undercard finally revealed ahead of comeback fight

The former two-time heavyweight champion is expected to return to the ring next week, before finally facing rival Tyson Fury later this year

View Image Anthony Joshua and Kristian Prenga face off ahead of their fight (Image: Dylan Hepworth/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Anthony Joshua will return to the ring next week, and the undercard for his fight with Kristian Prenga has finally been announced.

‌



The former two-time heavyweight will make a stunning comeback next weekend - seven months on from his near-death experience after being involved in a tragic car crash in Nigeria which resulted in the deaths of close friends Latif Ayodele and Sina Ghami.

‌



Joshua has not fought since his rather uninspiring sixth-round knockout victory over YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul last Christmas.

‌



Providing he comes away unscathed against Prenga, it will finally set up a long-awaited showdown with Tyson Fury. The 'Gypsy King' is expected to take on Poland's Mariusz Wach in Pattaya, Thailand, on July 24 - a day before Joshua's fight. It was recently announced that the 12 fights which will take place on the Joshua vs Prenga card over in Jeddah after some slight delay.

Oleksandr Usyk branded 'average' after retirement decision READ MORE :

‌



In the co-main event, Britain's Hamzah Sheeraz will defend his WBO super middleweight title for the first time against Simon Zachenhuber. The German scrapper suffered a shock defeat to Pawel Augustynik on the Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov undercard back in April, but got back to winning ways two months later after forcing Armin Ajrulai to quit.

Much to the surprise of many, Augustynik is set to fight on the same billing as Zachenhuber against undefeated Danish brawler Jacob Bank.

Sheeraz won the title back in May after brutally stopping Alem Begic at the Pyramids of Giza. Elsewhere on the card, Josh Kelly will make the first defence of his IBF super welterweight title against unbeaten Irish challenger Caoimhin Agyarko. The Sunderland native won the belt back in January following a unanimous decision victory over Bakhram Murtazaliev in January.

‌



Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury to be held at Wembley on one condition READ MORE :

Eddie Hall reveals next fight after Tommy Fury defeat READ MORE :

Exciting Japanese featherweight prospect Reito Tsutsumi is set to return to Saudi Arabia following impressive stoppage victory in Riyadh back in December. He will take on fellow undefeated fighter Alvino Herrera. Olympic gold medallist Oleksandr Khyzhniak will make the walk to the professional ring for the second time in his career.

The Ukrainian will take on Frenchman Lenny Patrach. British flyweight Mikie Tallon will make his return to action next weekend - with the Scouse scrapper clashing with Venezuela's Orlando Pino.

But all eyes will be on how Joshua fares on his return. The Brit revealed last month, he was even willing to return to a gruelling training camp much earlier, as he targets a statement victory in the Middle East before finally trading leather with Fury later this year.

‌



"Really about two months ago. I was training but there’s levels to training. Two months ago I started really ramping things up, so it’s been good. Pre camp has been solid, obviously getting fitter, stronger so I can push myself more. I’m in a good place for today," he said.

Mentally, Joshua was as ready as ever, but he just needed that extra time to get in peak physical condition. "Physically. Mentally, very strong. Mentally very strong. Physically just got to get yourself back to basically sparring," he continued.

"No because it’s my purpose. Boxing is not only good for the competitive side of things it’s quite therapeutic. It gives us purpose. That’s what it does for me and I think this is a place where … I know it is the place where I am most comfortable. It gives me a purpose in my life."

Sports.title: England legend says Three Lions can beat Argentina and lay the 'Hand of God' to rest
Sports.content:
England legend says Three Lions can beat Argentina and lay the 'Hand of God' to rest

EXCLUSIVE: Peter Reid, 70, famously tried to chase down Diego Maradona before he scored the second goal at the Azteca in Mexico in the 1986 World Cup quarter final. England meet their old foes at the World Cup in Wednesday's semi-final

View 4 Images England legend Peter Reid thinks we can win against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

England legend Peter Reid believes we can beat Argentina and lay the ghosts of 1986 to rest.

‌



Reid, 70, famously tried to chase down Diego Maradona before he scored the second goal at the Azteca in Mexico in the World Cup quarter final.

‌



England meet their old foes at the World Cup in Wednesday's semi-final. Reid told the Mirror : "Do I think we have enough? I think we will beat them.

‌



"We have not been great but we are finding a way. With Kane and Bellingham, you always have a chance. I know they have Messi, but I still think we will beat them.

"With Tuchel and Anthony Barry, and I know him very well, I think we will have enough to combat Messi. Look at the four teams in the semis; they are all quality sides. From the outside looking in, and knowing a little about it, England have a good spirit.

"Thomas Tuchel seems to get his substitutions right, I honestly believe they will beat them. In 1986, the group stages were in Monterrey, but the Paraguay game in Mexico and the match against Argentina were sensational.

‌



Was Thomas Tuchel right to criticise England after their win? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

View 4 Images Peter Reid, England legend, up against all-time great Maradona in Mexico in 1986 (Image: Getty Images)

"I have played in big games all over the world, but for political reasons that 1986 quarter-final was unbelievable. Was Maradona the best of all time? Dixie Dean, Tom Finney, Sir Stanley Edwards, Duncan Edwards, Messi, Di Stefano, George Best, Dennis Law - how do you compare?

"It is so difficult to say. I think Diego was absolutely outstanding, but it is impossible to say who was the best in the world." He added: "Now you have every game shown and analysed on social media; nowadays there is no physical contact in my opinion.

‌



"They are great athletes, but they do not have to face what the players did in my day. Howard Kendall used to tell me, 'Get into them early doors, get an early tackle in'.

"I used to say 'Gaffer, you say that every f***king week'. How would Messi deal with that now? With VAR, they have sanitised the game. I still love it, I still go, still watch it, and I am still passionate about it.

"I think France will beat Spain, and I am not sure if we will beat France in the final, but Kane and Bellingham are not bad - with them, we always have a chance. Bellingham's first goal against Norway was brilliant, his first touch was great. So we have a great chance of doing it."

‌



View 4 Images England legends Peter Reid and Terry Butcher (Image: PA)

The Argentine legend quipped that his first goal in their 2-1 victory in 1986 was “a little with the head of Maradona, a little with the hand of God”. His second was dubbed the ‘goal of the century’ when he dribbled past five England players and goalkeeper Peter Shilton to score the winner.

Tunisian Ali Bin Nasser sold the ball used in the 1986 game for £2m four years ago. England fought back with an 81st minute goal from Lineker which won him the tournament's 'Golden Boot' for top scorer. But Argentina went to win the tournament.

‌



View 4 Images The England team of 1986 (Image: Mirrorpix)

Bin Nasser said of the infamous Hand of God: "I couldn't see the incident clearly, Shilton and Maradona were facing me from behind. "As per FIFA instructions, I looked to my linesman for confirmation of the validity of the goal.

"He made his way back to the halfway line indicating he was satisfied that the goal should stand. At the end of the match the England head coach Bobby Robson said to me: 'You did a good job but the linesman was irresponsible'."

Article continues below

England face their toughest task yet when they meet the world champions, with superstar Messi. Reid added: "I would love them to do it. I think France will go through against Spain. And they will take some beating in the final."

Sports.title: 'Extraordinary, ordinary Jude Bellingham is the real deal'
Sports.content:
How do Jude Bellingham's critics square their claims that he is a petulant, disruptive influence on the England team with the trail he is blazing at the World Cup, shooting us to a showdown with Argentina in ­tomorrow’s semi-final?

For context: we’ve only made it this far three times before in World Cup history: 1966, 1990 and 2018. For even more context: Bellingham is the only player from any team to score two goals in a game in consecutive World Cup matches since Argentina legend Diego Maradona in 1990.

When you’re that good, you are fully entitled to call things as you see them. And there’s where it lies for Jude Bellingham’s critics. Left to them, footballers would still be sitting up straight in readiness for the manager’s arrival, shaking hands to celebrate a goal and nowhere near any campaigns to speak about mens’ vulnerabilities, ­preferring instead a stiff upper lip.

Bellingham’s haters remain stuck, knee deep, in an age when forelocks were tugged and caps were doffed in the face of sporting authority.

‌



View 4 Images Bellingham is fast becoming one of the greatest footballers of all time, says Darren (Image: Getty Images)

Bellingham has never, ever, ascribed to that kind of deference. Which is why his response to criticism of the England team’s performance against Norway, from head coach Thomas Tuchel, was to defend his team-mates.

It sent his critics into a frenzy. Yet even they must be struggling to square his standing up for his band of brothers with the idea that he’s a negative influence.

Either way, when you’re that good, you’re not worried about the consequences. In the same way that neither Kylian Mbappe nor, say, Lionel Messi would be worried about the repercussions of speaking their minds.

‌



Even as a player for the German club Borussia ­Dortmund, Bellingham has always oozed a confidence and a consistency to back up his talk with action.

View 4 Images Norway's Erling Braut Haaland congratulates England's Jude Bellingham as Norway's Fredrik Aursnes looks on (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Before Dortmund, teenage Bellingham was so amazing at his previous club, Birmingham City, that they decided no other player would wear his 22 shirt after he was sold.

At his current club, Real Madrid, ­Bellingham inspired his team-mates to the Spanish equivalent of the 2023-24 Premier League title and the FA Cup, as well as the Champions League – all in his debut season.

‌



At the European Championship Finals two years ago, it was Bellingham saving England with the winning goal against Serbia in the group stages and a match-saving goal against Slovakia.

And now, at this World Cup, Bellingham has scored in four of England’s six matches, saving the country on Saturday night after Norway had looked as though they’d cause a massive upset. Already, Bellingham is being spoken of as one of England’s greatest players of all time.

View 4 Images Darren says: Bellingham is an ordinary boy from Birmingham doing extraordinary things in the US and refusing to ­apologise for who he is (Image: AP Photo/Lynne Sladky)

He would prefer that to be on the basis of winning this World Cup rather than memories and a hard-luck semi-final story.

‌



That said, outside the heroes of 66, Bellingham is easily up alongside Gary Lineker, Alan Shearer, David Beckham, Michael Owen, Wayne Rooney and Harry Kane as a saviour of this nation when our major tournament future has been on the line.

Bellingham isn’t an Arthur Fery, the Wimbledon “Brit” semi-finalist who is actually the son of a French multimillionaire, football club owner and a member of the All England Club.

Bellingham is an ordinary boy from Birmingham doing extraordinary things in the US and refusing to ­apologise for who he is. He is the real inspiration to all of us. You’ll be agreeing when he scores the winner against Argentina tomorrow night.

Sports.title: Referee dropped for 2026 World Cup dies aged 38 after arrest
Sports.content:
Referee dropped for 2026 World Cup dies aged 38 after arrest

Rob Dieperink has died aged 38, weeks after the Dutch referee was stood down from going to the 2026 World Cup

View 2 Images FIFA referee Rob Dieperink has died aged 38. (Image: Photo by Pieter van der Woude/BSR Agency/Getty Images))

FIFA referee Rob Dieperink has passed away aged 38. The Eredivisie official, who was stood down from officiating at this summer's World Cup and dropped from their list of officials, was arrested back in April by the Metropolitan Police following allegations of sexual assault against an underage boy in London – a case which was later dropped.

‌



Dutch police are investigating Dieperink's death, with the cause unknown at this stage.

‌



The Dutch Football Association says it is "shocked and deeply saddened" by the passing of Dieperink. In a statement, they said: "We are shocked and deeply saddened by the passing of referee Rob Dieperink.

‌



"With Rob, the refereeing community loses a highly valued referee with international experience, but above all, a fine and dedicated colleague.

"Our thoughts go out to his family, friends, and everyone who held him dear. We wish them much strength and support in coping with this great loss."

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



Dieperink had been selected to feature at the 2026 World Cup among the Netherlands' contingent as a video assistant referee to accompany Danny Makkellie. However, in light of the news that he had been arrested following the allegation in England, he was stood down by the governing body.

The 38-year-old was taken into custody after an alleged incident in a London hotel following Crystal Palace's 3-0 win over Fiorentina, on suspicion of a sexual assault against a teenage boy.

Met Police confirmed to The Athletic in May that the case had been dropped as "the evidential threshold had not been met" and "no further action" would be taken.

‌



The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB), who employed Dieperink, backed the match official. While in a statement to Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf, the 38-year-old expressed disappointment in the decision from FIFA.

He said: "It makes me very sad that I have been wrongly accused. I fully cooperated with the police investigation and also immediately gave full openness to FIFA, UEFA and the KNVB.

“The allegations were refuted and the case was dismissed within two weeks after an adequate and thorough investigation by the police.

‌



“I am grateful for the support I have received from the KNVB and the way they have dealt with this case. It is a pity that FIFA has decided not to appoint me for the World Cup, I am of course disappointed about that.”

View 2 Images Dutch top-flight and FIFA referee Rob Dieperink has died aged 38. (Image: Photo by Broer van den Boom/BSR Agency/Getty Images)

The KNVB said in a statement, published by The Athletic: “We stand for a safe and honest football culture at all levels and always take reports of unwanted behaviour seriously.

‌



"Obviously, we think that a Dutch referee should be of unquestionable behaviour, but we also think it is important that he gets the chance to tell his story and not be wrongly accused.

“In this specific case, the police in the United Kingdom have investigated and closed the case. Rob Dieperink has cooperated fully and given openness to the KNVB from the very beginning, and based on all available information, we see no reason not to appoint him for matches in the Dutch league.”

Dieperink began refereeing in Holland's top-flight in 2017 and moved into the international stage as a video assistant, serving several matches during the European Championships in Germany in 2024.

Article continues below

He was in the middle for 84 Eredivisie matches with his final match coming during PEC Zwolle's 1-0 win over Heracles Almelo on May 3, 2026.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
